{
  "items": [
    {
      "questionId": "q7",
      "maxMarks": 4,
      "answer": {
        "marking": {
          "type": "additive",
          "points": [
            {
              "id": "1",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "The study demonstrates that the wording of a question (leading question) can alter memory for an event.",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["leading question", "wording", "alter memory"],
              "allow": ["change memory", "influence recall", "affect memory"],
              "reject": []
            },
            {
              "id": "2",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "The verb 'smashed' (Group A) implies greater speed and damage than 'contacted' (Group B).",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["smashed", "contacted", "implies", "greater speed", "damage"],
              "allow": ["suggests more force", "implies more severe collision"],
              "reject": []
            },
            {
              "id": "3",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "This led Group A to reconstruct their memory, reporting broken glass that was not present (misinformation effect).",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["reconstruct", "misinformation effect", "broken glass", "not present"],
              "allow": ["false memory", "incorporated misinformation", "memory distortion"],
              "reject": []
            },
            {
              "id": "4",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "This shows memory is not a perfect record but is susceptible to post-event information and suggestion.",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["not a perfect record", "susceptible", "post-event information", "suggestion"],
              "allow": ["memory is malleable", "influenced by external cues", "constructive process"],
              "reject": []
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "acceptableAlternatives": [
        "Any reference to Loftus and Palmer (1974) as the study.",
        "Mention of schema theory or reconstructive memory as an explanation.",
        "Use of terms like 'memory conformity' or 'source monitoring error' if correctly applied."
      ],
      "commonMistakes": [
        "Describing the study without linking it to the concept of leading questions.",
        "Confusing the effect with forgetting or decay.",
        "Stating that memory is always accurate or inaccurate without nuance.",
        "Using vague language like 'the question changed the answer' without specifying how."
      ]
    },
    {
      "questionId": "q8",
      "maxMarks": 16,
      "answer": {
        "marking": {
          "type": "additive",
          "points": [
            {
              "id": "1",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "The working memory model (Baddeley and Hitch, 1974) is a multi-component model of short-term memory.",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["working memory model", "Baddeley and Hitch", "multi-component", "short-term memory"],
              "allow": ["STM", "short-term store"],
              "reject": []
            },
            {
              "id": "2",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "The central executive is the most important component; it controls attention and coordinates the other components.",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["central executive", "controls attention", "coordinates"],
              "allow": ["directs attention", "manages resources", "allocates tasks"],
              "reject": []
            },
            {
              "id": "3",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "The phonological loop processes auditory information and has two parts: the phonological store (inner ear) and articulatory process (inner voice).",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["phonological loop", "auditory information", "phonological store", "articulatory process"],
              "allow": ["inner ear", "inner voice", "verbal/acoustic information"],
              "reject": []
            },
            {
              "id": "4",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "The visuo-spatial sketchpad processes visual and spatial information; it has a visual cache and inner scribe.",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["visuo-spatial sketchpad", "visual", "spatial", "visual cache", "inner scribe"],
              "allow": ["visual information", "spatial information", "visual store"],
              "reject": []
            },
            {
              "id": "5",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "The episodic buffer (added later, 2000) is a temporary store that integrates information from the other components and long-term memory.",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["episodic buffer", "integrates", "long-term memory"],
              "allow": ["links to LTM", "combines information", "temporary store"],
              "reject": []
            },
            {
              "id": "6",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "Evidence from dual-task performance supports the model: people can perform two tasks simultaneously if they use different components (e.g., visual and verbal).",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["dual-task", "different components", "simultaneously"],
              "allow": ["concurrent tasks", "interference", "multiple tasks"],
              "reject": []
            },
            {
              "id": "7",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "Evidence from brain-damaged patients (e.g., KF) supports separate components: KF had impaired phonological loop but intact visuo-spatial sketchpad.",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["KF", "brain-damaged", "impaired phonological loop", "intact visuo-spatial sketchpad"],
              "allow": ["case study", "neuropsychological evidence", "dissociation"],
              "reject": []
            },
            {
              "id": "8",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "The model is supported by its ability to explain everyday memory tasks (e.g., reading, mental arithmetic).",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["everyday memory tasks", "reading", "mental arithmetic"],
              "allow": ["practical applications", "real-life examples"],
              "reject": []
            },
            {
              "id": "9",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "Evaluation: The model is based on laboratory research, which may lack ecological validity.",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["laboratory research", "ecological validity"],
              "allow": ["artificial tasks", "lack of real-world applicability"],
              "reject": []
            },
            {
              "id": "10",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "Evaluation: The central executive is not well-defined; it is vague and difficult to test empirically.",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["central executive", "vague", "difficult to test"],
              "allow": ["not well-explained", "lack of clarity", "hard to operationalize"],
              "reject": []
            },
            {
              "id": "11",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "Evaluation: The model is based on a limited range of participants (e.g., mostly Western, educated).",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["limited range", "participants", "Western", "educated"],
              "allow": ["cultural bias", "sample bias", "lack of diversity"],
              "reject": []
            },
            {
              "id": "12",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "Evaluation: The model does not fully explain how information is transferred to long-term memory.",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["transfer", "long-term memory", "not fully explain"],
              "allow": ["LTM", "encoding", "storage"],
              "reject": []
            },
            {
              "id": "13",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "Evaluation: The model is supported by neuroimaging studies showing different brain areas for different components.",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["neuroimaging", "brain areas", "different components"],
              "allow": ["fMRI", "brain scans", "neural evidence"],
              "reject": []
            },
            {
              "id": "14",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "Evaluation: The model is flexible and can be updated (e.g., addition of episodic buffer).",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["flexible", "updated", "episodic buffer"],
              "allow": ["adaptable", "revised", "evolved"],
              "reject": []
            },
            {
              "id": "15",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "Evaluation: The model may oversimplify memory; it does not account for individual differences or emotional factors.",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["oversimplify", "individual differences", "emotional factors"],
              "allow": ["simplistic", "does not consider", "lack of complexity"],
              "reject": []
            },
            {
              "id": "16",
              "marks": 1,
              "code": "M",
              "text": "Overall, the model is a useful framework for understanding short-term memory but has limitations in explaining all aspects of memory.",
              "dep": [],
              "ft": false,
              "essentialTerms": ["useful framework", "limitations", "short-term memory"],
              "allow": ["valuable model", "has strengths and weaknesses", "not comprehensive"],
              "reject": []
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "acceptableAlternatives": [
        "Any reference to other researchers (e.g., Baddeley, 2000; Shallice and Warrington, 1970) for evidence.",
        "Use of terms like 'working memory' instead of 'short-term memory' where appropriate.",
        "Discussion of the model's application to real-world tasks (e.g., driving, learning).",
        "Mention of alternative models (e.g., Atkinson and Shiffrin) for comparison, if relevant."
      ],
      "commonMistakes": [
        "Describing the model without evaluation or evidence.",
        "Confusing the components (e.g., mixing up phonological loop and visuo-spatial sketchpad).",
        "Failing to mention the episodic buffer or its role.",
        "Using vague or unsupported evaluation (e.g., 'the model is good' without specifics).",
        "Not linking evidence to the model's components."
      ]
    }
  ]
}
